title: Hyperscaler nuclear PPA wave for AI datacenters pulls the whole fuel cycle forward
hypothesis: AI power demand drives a second, larger wave of hyperscaler nuclear power agreements and equity investments into SMR developers, pulling forward the entire fuel-cycle demand curve.

chain.cause: Hyperscalers sign PPAs and take equity stakes in advanced-reactor developers to secure firm clean power
chain.effect: SMR and advanced-reactor equities rerate on backlog and credible offtake
chain.rationale: Datacenter demand supplies the missing customer for pre-revenue reactor developers; a validated offtake is the catalyst that reprices them.

chain.cause: A larger committed reactor pipeline lifts forward fuel and enrichment demand
chain.effect: Fuel-cycle incumbents get pulled up alongside the developers
chain.rationale: Every new reactor is a multi-decade fuel buyer; the demand signal flows back to miners and enrichers even before steel is poured.

chain.cause: Firm-baseload procurement for power-hungry compute reinforces the domestic energy-security narrative
chain.effect: Defense-adjacent microreactor and resilient-power programs attract parallel federal funding
chain.rationale: The same AI-power scarcity that drives hyperscaler PPAs routes DoD base-power and microreactor dollars to the primes, a non-obvious secondary bid.

playbook.rationale: Most direct beneficiary of datacenter PPAs and hyperscaler equity interest.
Furthest-along SMR platform to convert AI-power demand into orders.
Owns fuel and Westinghouse reactor tech, capturing the downstream demand pull.
Basket exposure to the sector-wide fuel-cycle rerate.

title: Utility uncovered-requirements cliff ignites a term-contracting wave that breaks the price higher
hypothesis: Utilities that under-contracted through the bear market face a wall of uncovered 2028+ requirements and are forced into a replacement-rate contracting cycle that breaks the term price higher and drags spot with it.

chain.cause: Utilities must contract for post-2028 fuel they have not covered, at a pace above annual burn
chain.effect: Term price breaks out and pulls spot with it, rerating producers on contracted revenue visibility
chain.rationale: The term market, not spot, is where utilities actually buy; a contracting wave is the highest-conviction structural driver and rewards names with uncommitted pounds.

chain.cause: Higher, durable term prices make restart and greenfield economics work
chain.effect: Restart and development names sign contracts and secure financing
chain.rationale: Long-dated contracts at incentive prices are the trigger that converts development ounces into funded production.

playbook.rationale: Largest pool of uncommitted, contract-leverage pounds among Western majors.
Cleanest way to own the sector-wide term-price rerate.
Restart optionality that only monetizes at the higher contracted prices this scenario creates.

title: Shadow-fleet sanctions enforcement tightens the compliant tanker pool
hypothesis: Escalating OFAC/EU designations of Russian and Iranian dark-fleet tankers strand aging tonnage and force cargoes onto the compliant fleet, spiking crude and product rates.

chain.cause: New tranches of shadow tankers lose insurance/port access and go idle
chain.effect: Compliant VLCC and product-tanker demand jumps as displaced barrels rebook on mainstream tonnage, lifting spot rates
chain.rationale: Frontline and DHT (VLCC), INSW (mixed), and Scorpio (products) capture the direct rate spike as an estimated 800+ shadow vessels face removal from effective supply.

chain.cause: Longer, less-efficient compliant routings raise effective ton-mile and delivered crude cost
chain.effect: More expensive oil logistics reinforces the energy-security case for nuclear baseload
chain.rationale: Tighter/more expensive oil logistics feeds the energy-security case for nuclear; a soft, sentiment-level ripple rather than a mechanical link.

playbook.rationale: Pure VLCC leverage to spot rates with a high-payout dividend policy.
Clean-balance-sheet VLCC play, direct spot exposure.
Product tankers benefit as refined-product flows re-route around sanctioned tonnage.
Energy-security spillover; small speculative sizing only.

title: DJI/Autel land on the FCC Covered List, forcing domestic drone reshoring across defense and precision-ag
hypothesis: The Countering CCP Drones Act pathway culminates in DJI and Autel being blocked from new US authorizations, creating a demand vacuum only domestic Blue UAS makers can fill across both military and agricultural markets.

chain.cause: DJI/Autel added to FCC Covered List or denied new equipment authorizations
chain.effect: US public-safety, enterprise and DoD buyers are forced onto domestic NDAA-compliant platforms, handing the thin small-cap supply base pricing power and multi-year backlog
chain.rationale: Red Cat (Teal/SRR-winner) and AeroVironment are the most direct Blue UAS-listed beneficiaries of a forced switch away from ~75% Chinese market share.

chain.cause: Domestic makers cannot scale fast enough to absorb the demand step-change
chain.effect: The scarcity narrative re-rates the whole domestic small-UAS cohort even before revenue lands
chain.rationale: Multiple compression on 'only compliant supplier' scarcity historically front-runs actual order flow in this cohort.

chain.cause: DJI Agras spraying drones (dominant in US precision-ag application) are also caught by the ban
chain.effect: Disruption to aerial crop-spraying pushes growers toward ground-based precision equipment while a BVLOS unlock hands the ag-drone TAM to US makers
chain.rationale: Non-obvious ripple: DJI owns most of the US ag-drone spraying fleet, so a ban is a tailwind for Deere's See & Spray ground-application franchise and the domestic autonomy stack.

chain.cause: FAA BVLOS rulemaking plus a Chinese-hardware vacuum unlocks scaled autonomous ag spraying
chain.effect: US small-drone makers gain a dual defense-plus-agriculture addressable market
chain.rationale: Beyond-visual-line-of-sight approval is the regulatory unlock making commercial ag drone fleets viable, layering ag demand on top of the military reshoring for the same airframes.

playbook.rationale: Highest-beta domestic pure-play; SRR win plus ban equals order visibility across defense and ag.
Compliant, scaled, and diversified across the compliant-drone stack including BVLOS-enabled ag.
Secondary compliant-supplier scarcity beneficiary.
Cross-domain lever on ag-spraying reshoring toward ground equipment and domestic autonomy.

title: Debt-maturity wall forces a distressed M&A wave that reshapes the operator landscape
hypothesis: 2026-2027 debt maturities without banking reform force weaker operators into fire-sale consolidation, bifurcating winners from the distressed.

chain.cause: Heavily-levered operators cannot refinance 2026-2027 maturities at viable rates absent SAFER banking
chain.effect: Distressed operators sell assets or file; well-capitalized operators acquire share cheaply, widening the winner/loser gap
chain.rationale: This is a dispersion trade, not a directional one: strong balance sheets (GTBIF, TCNNF) consolidate while weak names dilute or fail; MSOS as a basket is mixed.

chain.cause: Consolidation concentrates market share in the survivors, improving pricing power and margins
chain.effect: Surviving operators re-rate on cleaner competitive dynamics and accretive acquisitions
chain.rationale: Fewer, stronger players in mature state markets historically stabilizes wholesale pricing and improves unit economics for survivors.

chain.cause: A visible distress cycle chills speculative capital, keeping the broad complex and Canadian LPs under pressure until reform arrives
chain.effect: Canadian LPs and the levered basket stay depressed as risk appetite for the sector shrinks
chain.rationale: A public distress narrative suppresses sector sentiment and keeps cost of capital high for everyone lacking a fortress balance sheet.

playbook.rationale: Balance-sheet strength positions it as an acquirer of distressed assets at attractive prices.
Low-leverage Florida-anchored operator that survives and consolidates.
Basket exposure includes the levered names most at risk in a maturity-wall squeeze; dispersion favors singles over the ETF.
Chronically cash-burning Canadian LP most exposed to a risk-off sector sentiment shift.

title: Black Sea breadbasket rupture and grain/fertilizer export cutoff
hypothesis: A collapse of the Black Sea grain corridor plus sanctions/retaliation cutting Russian-Belarusian potash and ammonia exports triggers a global food-and-fertilizer crisis, rerouting dry bulk, driving NATO defense spend, and firming uranium via Russian gas retaliation.

chain.cause: Black Sea corridor collapse and Russia/Belarus potash-ammonia export cutoff
chain.effect: Grain and fertilizer prices spike; ex-Russia potash and nitrogen producers gain pricing power and share while grain merchandisers benefit from volatility and rerouted flows
chain.rationale: Russia/Belarus dominate potash and ammonia exports and the Black Sea is a top grain corridor; cutting both is the single most bullish supply shock for Western fertilizer and grains, with ADM gaining from merchandising volatility.

chain.cause: Rerouting of grain and fertilizer away from the Black Sea lengthens voyages and tightens dry-bulk tonnage
chain.effect: Dry-bulk shipping rates rise on longer ton-miles as cargoes source from the Americas/Australia
chain.rationale: Sourcing from farther origins lengthens ton-miles and tightens dry-bulk supply, a classic ton-mile-expansion leg that ag-only desks overlook.

chain.cause: NATO-Russia escalation around the Black Sea/Baltic drives European rearmament
chain.effect: Defense primes and drone/ISR names rally on accelerated NATO procurement and munitions restocking
chain.rationale: Deeper NATO-Russia confrontation drives European air-defense and munitions plus battlefield drones; ITA captures the broad rearmament re-rating.

chain.cause: Russian energy retaliation (gas cutoff to Europe) revives the energy-security push for nuclear
chain.effect: Uranium producers and enrichers firm on renewed baseload-security demand and reduced Rosatom fuel-cycle reliance
chain.rationale: A gas cutoff pushes Europe toward nuclear baseload and away from Russian fuel-cycle dependence, the leg ag desks never connect.

playbook.rationale: Most direct beneficiary of a Russian/Belarusian potash cutoff; pricing power and share gains are immediate and large.
Diversified potash and nitrogen leader capturing both fertilizer legs with liquidity to size.
Dry-bulk owner leveraged to ton-mile expansion as sourcing shifts to distant origins.
Broad exposure to European/NATO rearmament without single-name risk.
Energy-security nuclear beneficiary if Russian gas/fuel-cycle retaliation revives the European baseload push.

title: Sulfuric acid shortage forces Kazatomprom ISR cuts and squeezes phosphate fertilizer
hypothesis: A tightening sulfuric-acid market in Kazakhstan (the reagent that leaches uranium in in-situ recovery) caps Kazatomprom output below plan, tightening spot uranium while simultaneously squeezing phosphate fertilizers that compete for the same acid.

chain.cause: Kazatomprom cannot secure enough sulfuric acid to develop new wellfields and cuts production guidance
chain.effect: The world's lowest-cost, largest single source (~40% of primary supply) underdelivers, tightening the spot market and rerating producers
chain.rationale: A supply cut from the marginal swing producer is the single most powerful lever on uranium price; established producers with growing volumes capture the upside.

chain.cause: The same sulfuric acid Kazatomprom needs is the primary input for phosphoric acid used in DAP/MAP fertilizer
chain.effect: Acid scarcity raises phosphate producers' input costs and pinches margins even as it can support finished DAP prices
chain.rationale: Non-obvious cross-domain competition for the same reagent; the cost pass-through is imperfect, so margins compress before prices catch up.

chain.cause: Persistent Kazakh underdelivery pushes utilities to lock Western supply
chain.effect: Development-stage and restart names get contracted and financed
chain.rationale: A structural supply gap flows down the cost curve to higher-cost Western developers that only work at elevated prices.

playbook.rationale: Best liquidity and volume growth to monetize a spot tightening driven by Kazakh cuts.
Basket exposure captures the sector rerate without single-name execution risk.
High-beta Western producer leveraged to the sustained gap and utility contracting.
Phosphate margin squeeze from acid competition is the underappreciated cross-domain casualty.

title: Major cyber/kinetic attack on Western power grid and energy infrastructure
hypothesis: A state-linked cyber or sabotage campaign disables regional grid infrastructure and pipelines, exposing baseload fragility and AI-datacenter power scarcity, forcing an emergency pivot to firm nuclear baseload while disrupting fertilizer production and driving defense/cyber spend.

chain.cause: Grid attack plus AI-datacenter demand expose baseload fragility, triggering an emergency policy pivot to firm nuclear power
chain.effect: Uranium producers, enrichers and especially SMR developers rally hard on accelerated permitting and datacenter power-purchase demand
chain.rationale: A grid-security crisis is the strongest catalyst for firm baseload, fusing the AI-power-demand and energy-security narratives; SMR/OKLO get the sharpest re-rate, CCJ/UEC/LEU on fuel-cycle security.

chain.cause: State-linked attack on critical infrastructure drives urgent cyber, hardened-comms and resilience spending
chain.effect: Defense, cyber, and resilient space/ISR communications names rally as governments harden critical infrastructure
chain.rationale: Grid attacks drive cyber-defense and resilient PNT/comms budgets; hardened space comms and geospatial intel benefit as terrestrial infrastructure is shown vulnerable.

chain.cause: Energy price spike and grid instability disrupt electricity-intensive ammonia/nitrogen fertilizer production
chain.effect: Fertilizer output curtails on power constraints, tightening supply and lifting nitrogen/potash pricing
chain.rationale: Nitrogen fertilizer is highly energy-intensive; power-price spikes curtail production and hand pricing power to producers able to keep running.

chain.cause: Energy dislocation and rerouted fuel flows tighten seaborne energy logistics
chain.effect: Tanker rates firm on emergency crude/product imports and rerouting to backfill regional energy shortfalls
chain.rationale: Regional energy shortfalls drive emergency imports and rerouting, a second-order but real leg as physical energy scrambles to backfill the grid gap.

playbook.rationale: Highest-torque expression of the emergency pivot to firm, secure baseload for datacenters and grid resilience.
Core beneficiary of critical-infrastructure hardening, cyber and resilient-comms spending; liquid, lower-beta anchor.
Large-cap fuel-supply security beneficiary that institutions can size; steadier complement to volatile SMR developers.
Nitrogen producer with pricing power as electricity-intensive fertilizer output curtails.
Product tanker leg captures emergency refined-fuel imports and rerouting.

title: Record 2026-27 containership deliveries create a structural capacity glut
hypothesis: The historically large containership orderbook delivers into softening demand, eroding freight and charter rates for spot-exposed operators while charter-backed lessors stay insulated.

chain.cause: Newbuild deliveries outpace trade-volume growth
chain.effect: Idling and cascading of tonnage erodes spot freight and vessel earnings for spot-exposed operators
chain.rationale: ZIM's asset-light chartered model and spot exposure make it the prime loser in an oversupplied box market.

chain.cause: Lessors hold multi-year charters signed at elevated rates
chain.effect: Danaos and GSL earn contracted cashflow and relatively outperform even as the underlying market weakens
chain.rationale: The nuance generalists miss: a container glut is bearish operators but merely a slow renewal-rate headwind for backlog-covered lessors.

chain.cause: Lower ocean freight cost flows into commodity logistics
chain.effect: Cheaper container/bulk freight marginally eases delivered cost for ag traders
chain.rationale: Lower freight is a small tailwind to grain merchandising margins but not a primary driver; noted as context.

playbook.rationale: Direct earnings hit from box oversupply; thin margin of safety at spot troughs.
Contracted backlog and cheap valuation cushion downside; not a short.
Charter cover protects dividend near-term; monitor 2027 renewal exposure.

title: Global stagflation / sustained higher-for-longer rate regime splits every watchlist
hypothesis: A resurgence of inflation forces central banks to hold rates higher-for-longer or hike again, crushing long-duration, cash-burning speculative names while rewarding hard-asset commodity cash-flow across ag, uranium and shipping.

chain.cause: Higher-for-longer rates and rising discount rates crush long-duration, pre-revenue, retail-momentum equities
chain.effect: Speculative space and emerging-defense names with distant cash flows and dilution risk de-rate sharply
chain.rationale: The cash-burning capital-intensive space cohort and small-cap drone names rely on equity issuance and carry valuations built on out-year cash flows; this splits the defense domain, primes hold up while speculatives fall.

chain.cause: Risk-off in speculative retail growth plus tighter capital access hits the cannabis complex
chain.effect: Cannabis producers and MSOs, already cash-strained and capital-market-dependent, sell off hard on funding and dilution fears
chain.rationale: Cannabis is a high-beta, retail-sentiment, capital-market-dependent complex with chronic cash burn, precisely the profile destroyed in a higher-rate regime.

chain.cause: Commodity-led inflation and hard-asset rotation reward real-asset producers with near-term cash flow
chain.effect: Fertilizer and ag-commodity names catch a bid as an inflation hedge with real cash generation
chain.rationale: In a stagflationary regime cash-generative fertilizer and grain names are classic real-asset hedges that outperform long-duration growth.

chain.cause: Investors rotate into commodity cash-flow and inflation-beneficiary hard assets
chain.effect: Shipping real-asset spot cash flow and established uranium producers outperform while pre-cash-flow SMR developers lag
chain.rationale: Tanker and dry-bulk owners are real assets throwing off spot cash returnable as dividends, attractive in an inflationary rotation, in contrast with rate-sensitive pre-revenue SMR names.

playbook.rationale: Cleanest short-basket expression of the rate-shock hit to cash-burning, retail-driven cannabis.
Best liquid hard-asset inflation hedge with real cash flow and dividends; core long for the commodity side.
High-multiple, cash-burning, dilution-dependent space name most exposed to duration de-rating.
Real-asset shipping cash flow returned as dividends; performs as a tangible-asset inflation play.
Pre-revenue SMR developer with far-out cash flows; the rate-sensitive short leg within the otherwise-bullish uranium theme.

title: Cameco-owned Westinghouse lands a wave of AP1000 new-build orders
hypothesis: European and allied-Asian energy-security policy converts into firm AP1000 reactor orders, and the market underappreciates that Cameco's 49% Westinghouse stake gives CCJ direct reactor-vendor earnings on top of fuel demand.

chain.cause: Allied governments award AP1000 new-build contracts (Poland, Bulgaria, Ukraine, others) to Westinghouse
chain.effect: Cameco booms twice via its Westinghouse equity earnings and via multi-decade fuel offtake for the new fleet
chain.rationale: Underfollowed dual exposure: the market prices CCJ as a miner and misses the reactor-vendor earnings stream from the Westinghouse stake.

chain.cause: New Western reactor fleet must be fueled with non-Russian enriched uranium and conversion
chain.effect: Conversion and enrichment capacity gets long-term demand from the fuel-cycle midstream
chain.rationale: New AP1000s lock in decades of SWU and conversion demand, benefiting the Western midstream that avoids Russian supply.

chain.cause: Nuclear reframed as allied industrial and energy-security policy
chain.effect: Broad defense/energy-security policy tailwind for the nuclear supply chain
chain.rationale: Reactor exports become a geopolitical instrument; a supportive but diffuse tailwind rather than a direct earnings driver.

playbook.rationale: Only listed name with both fuel leverage and direct Westinghouse reactor-vendor earnings, an underpriced combination.
New Western fleet needs non-Russian enrichment, a multi-decade demand lock.
US conversion optionality benefits from an expanding Western fuel-cycle requirement.

title: 45Z credit and SAF mandates ignite a corn/soy-oil feedstock demand supercycle
hypothesis: Implementation of the 45Z clean-fuel production credit plus sustainable aviation fuel offtake pulls corn ethanol and soybean oil into energy markets, tightening feedstock balances and expanding crush margins.

chain.cause: Biofuel policy pulls soybean oil and corn ethanol into the energy complex
chain.effect: Feedstock balances tighten, crush margins expand, and processors and grain firm
chain.rationale: ADM and BG are the largest US oilseed crushers; 45Z and SAF demand structurally lift crush spreads and corn/soyoil pricing.

chain.cause: Higher crop prices lift farmer income
chain.effect: Stronger equipment capex and farm-sector sentiment
chain.rationale: Farm income is the primary driver of large-equipment replacement cycles, benefiting Deere and the broad ag ETF.

chain.cause: Feedstock imports (used cooking oil, tallow) surge to fill renewable-diesel demand
chain.effect: Product and chemical tanker demand rises on long-haul feedstock trade
chain.rationale: Renewable diesel plants pull imported UCO and tallow on product/chem tankers, a non-obvious tonne-mile tailwind.

playbook.rationale: Largest lever to crush-margin expansion from SAF and renewable-diesel feedstock demand.
Global oilseed crusher directly benefiting from tightening soyoil balances.
Ethanol demand pull supports corn pricing.
Product tanker beneficiary of rising imported biofuel-feedstock flows.

title: HALEU bottleneck strangles advanced-reactor deployment and rewards the sole enricher
hypothesis: With Russian HALEU banned and Centrus the only licensed US producer, high-assay low-enriched uranium becomes the binding constraint on advanced reactors, rewarding the enricher while delaying deployers and pulling in defense-microreactor funding.

chain.cause: Advanced-reactor fuel demand outruns the only domestic HALEU cascade, with no Russian backstop
chain.effect: Centrus wins expanded DOE offtake and pricing power while SMR/Oklo deployment timelines slip on fuel availability
chain.rationale: Centrus (LEU) is a near-monopoly chokepoint; scarcity of the input it uniquely makes is directly bullish for it even as it is a headwind for fuel-hungry deployers.

chain.cause: DoD microreactor programs (Project Pele, base power) compete for the same scarce HALEU and accelerate federal funding
chain.effect: Defense-adjacent nuclear and microreactor names attract government dollars and offtake
chain.rationale: Energy-security framing routes DoD budget into the fuel-supply chain; primes with microreactor/nuclear exposure are the listed beneficiaries.

chain.cause: Enrichment expansion and new cascades get funded to close the gap
chain.effect: Centrus capacity buildout is de-risked and constrained deployers become buyable as the bottleneck clears
chain.rationale: Once fuel supply is secured, the same deployers that were constrained become buyable as the bottleneck clears.

playbook.rationale: Sole domestic HALEU producer captures scarcity rent and DOE contracts directly.
Fuel constraint is a near-term timeline risk but long-term demand pull; hold through the gap.
Defense microreactor programs channel federal funding into the fuel-cycle chokepoint.

title: Golden Dome missile shield funds a space-based sensor and interceptor layer
hypothesis: The homeland missile-defense architecture is funded around a proliferated space layer, pulling forward smallsat, launch, targets and interceptor demand, with a non-obvious power tail into nuclear microreactors.

chain.cause: DoD funds a proliferated space sensor/interceptor layer with recurring launch cadence
chain.effect: Launch providers, smallsat ISR and prime integrators book multi-year architecture work
chain.rationale: Rocket Lab (launch plus Photon buses), Planet (persistent ISR/tracking), and the primes are the natural architecture winners.

chain.cause: Target-drone and hypersonic-test demand plus cadence pressure
chain.effect: Test-and-targets and responsive launch names get a distinct funding line
chain.rationale: Kratos supplies hypersonic test vehicles and targets; every interceptor program needs a target/launch pipeline.

chain.cause: Power-hungry radar/directed-energy sats and hardened ground stations need dense, resilient power
chain.effect: Space nuclear microreactors and ground SMR power become part of the deterrence buildout
chain.rationale: Non-obvious tail: a space-based defense layer is a power problem; microreactor and HALEU suppliers ride the same appropriations wave.

playbook.rationale: Cadence and vertical integration make it the small-cap architecture linchpin.
Prime integrator leverage on the interceptor/sensor stack with lower beta.
Targets/hypersonic test pull-through.
Cross-domain power tail on a space-based buildout.

title: DEA final rule moves cannabis to Schedule III, unlocking 280E relief across the complex
hypothesis: The stalled DEA administrative-law-judge process resolves and a final Schedule III rule publishes, unlocking 280E tax relief for the entire complex.

chain.cause: DEA publishes final rule reclassifying cannabis to Schedule III
chain.effect: 280E tax burden lifts, freeing cash flow for US multi-state operators and re-rating the complex on improved economics
chain.rationale: Schedule III removes the 280E prohibition on ordinary business deductions, the single largest structural drag on US operator profitability; MSOS and the profitable MSOs benefit most.

chain.cause: Improved after-tax cash flow lets operators fund expansion and pay down debt, reducing distress-sale risk
chain.effect: Canadian LPs with US optionality re-rate as the US federal path de-risks their footprint strategy
chain.rationale: Canadian names trade partly as a call option on eventual US access; a concrete federal step tightens that optionality into value.

chain.cause: Cannabis normalization expands legal cultivation acreage and greenhouse input demand
chain.effect: Fertilizer and ag-input names see a marginal demand tailwind
chain.rationale: Large-scale legal cultivation is nutrient-intensive; a durable US legal market is a small but real incremental demand source for potash and nitrogen.

playbook.rationale: Cleanest levered expression of US operators receiving 280E relief across the whole MSO complex.
Profitable, well-capitalized MSO where removing 280E flows directly to net income.
High-tax-drag operator that gains disproportionately from deductibility.
Re-rates on US optionality de-risking, secondary to direct US operators.

title: China quarantine/blockade of Taiwan and trade weaponization
hypothesis: A PLA quarantine or blockade of Taiwan freezes transpacific container/dry-bulk trade, triggers export controls and global risk-off, and prompts China to weaponize dominance in critical inputs and processed nuclear fuel-cycle supply, cross-cutting shipping, defense, uranium and agriculture.
triggers: China rare-earth or fuel-cycle export restriction

chain.cause: PLA blockade/quarantine halts shipping through the Taiwan Strait and transpacific lanes
chain.effect: Container liners and dry-bulk rates whipsaw: initial spike on rerouting and congestion, with two-sided demand-destruction risk if global trade seizes
chain.rationale: Container rates spike on strait avoidance and Asian port congestion while a true blockade destroys volume; ZIM and lessors are the sharpest but two-sided movers, dry bulk reacts to disrupted iron-ore/grain flows.

chain.cause: Great-power crisis in the Pacific forces allied rearmament and Indo-Pacific procurement surge
chain.effect: Defense primes, space/ISR, and drone/counter-drone names rally on Pacific deterrence spending and munitions restocking
chain.rationale: A Taiwan crisis is the central scenario driving US/Japan/Australia defense budgets: long-range fires, munitions, attritable drones and resilient space comms/ISR.

chain.cause: China weaponizes control of processed nuclear fuel-cycle and enrichment supply as economic leverage
chain.effect: Western uranium producers and domestic enrichers rally on supply-security fears and fuel-cycle reshoring
chain.rationale: A China trade rupture reinforces the West's push to onshore conversion/enrichment; LEU and UUUU are direct reshoring beneficiaries, CCJ/UEC on the supply-security premium.

chain.cause: Global risk-off and disrupted transpacific grain/fertilizer flows tighten ag-input logistics
chain.effect: Fertilizer and grain-handling names react to disrupted Pacific trade and food-security stockpiling; potash/nitrogen pricing firms
chain.rationale: Disrupted Pacific bulk trade snarls grain merchandising and fertilizer flows; food-security stockpiling firms potash/nitrogen while DBA captures ag-commodity inflation.

playbook.rationale: Broad, liquid defense exposure to Pacific rearmament without single-name headline risk; the most durable leg.
Direct beneficiary of fuel-cycle reshoring if China/Russia enrichment access is cut; asymmetric on supply-security policy.
Highest-beta container play for the initial rate spike; size small given two-sided demand-destruction risk.
Attritable drones and target systems central to Pacific deterrence procurement.
Diversified potash/nitrogen producer that benefits from food-security stockpiling and firm pricing.

title: Strait of Hormuz closure after Iran-Israel escalation
hypothesis: A hot military exchange between Israel/US and Iran leads Iran to mine or blockade the Strait of Hormuz, choking ~20% of seaborne oil and much LNG/LPG, spiking tanker rates and energy prices, inflating fertilizer feedstock, bidding uranium as an energy-security hedge and rallying defense on a live war.
triggers: Israeli or US strike on Natanz/Fordow
IRGC Hormuz closure or tanker seizure/mining
OPEC spare capacity unable to reroute around the strait

chain.cause: Iran mines/blockades the Strait of Hormuz following military escalation
chain.effect: Crude and product tanker spot rates spike as vessels reroute, tonnage is stranded and war-risk premiums explode
chain.rationale: Tanker owners are the most direct beneficiaries: ton-mile demand jumps as barrels reroute around Africa and war-risk pricing power surges; FRO/DHT are pure crude plays, STNG/INSW carry products with spot leverage.

chain.cause: Oil and natural gas prices spike on the supply shock
chain.effect: Gas feedstock for ammonia/nitrogen inflates, tightening global ammonia supply and handing ex-region producers pricing power
chain.rationale: Gulf gas disruption tightens global ammonia supply (the Middle East is a major low-cost nitrogen exporter); ex-region producers gain relative pricing power while DBA captures ag-commodity inflation.

chain.cause: Energy-security panic and fear of hydrocarbon weaponization drives a structural bid for nuclear baseload
chain.effect: Uranium miners, enrichers and SMR developers rally as the nuclear-as-energy-security narrative accelerates
chain.rationale: A weaponized-hydrocarbon shock is the cleanest bull case for uranium: it reframes nuclear from climate play to security imperative.

chain.cause: Active Middle East shooting war with US carrier involvement
chain.effect: Defense primes and munitions/drone/ISR names rally on restocking, air-defense demand and elevated procurement expectations
chain.rationale: A live regional war drives missile-defense interceptors, loitering munitions and drone demand; the most consensus leg but timing and magnitude are routinely underestimated.

playbook.rationale: Purest, most immediate leverage to a Hormuz tanker-rate spike with high operating leverage to day rates.
Best liquid vehicle for the energy-security-into-nuclear structural bid that institutions can size.
Nitrogen producer that gains pricing power as Gulf ammonia supply is disrupted.
Air-defense and interceptor restocking beneficiary; lower-beta way to hold the defense leg.
Product tanker leg captures refined-product dislocation and rerouting in addition to crude.

title: European gas spike curtails EU nitrogen output, handing pricing power to US low-cost producers
hypothesis: A cold winter or renewed Russian gas cutoff spikes European TTF prices, making ammonia synthesis uneconomic and curtailing EU nitrogen capacity, tightening the global urea/UAN balance in favor of gas-advantaged US producers.

chain.cause: European TTF gas spikes above ammonia breakeven, forcing EU nitrogen curtailments
chain.effect: Global urea/UAN/ammonia prices rally and US Gulf gas-advantaged producers capture wide margins
chain.rationale: CF is a pure-play US natural-gas-fed nitrogen producer; its cost-curve gap versus curtailed European supply widens dramatically when TTF spikes.

chain.cause: Nitrogen input costs jump for global farmers
chain.effect: Reduced fertilizer application and acreage shifts raise yield risk, firming the grain complex
chain.rationale: Under-fertilized crops lower expected yields, a lagged bullish push into grain futures.

chain.cause: Acute gas-dependency shock revives European energy-security and baseload-nuclear urgency
chain.effect: Accelerated nuclear buildout narrative and uranium demand expectations
chain.rationale: Repeated gas-driven industrial curtailments strengthen the political case for nuclear baseload, a durable tailwind for the uranium complex.

playbook.rationale: Highest-beta beneficiary of European nitrogen curtailment given US gas cost advantage.
Diversified N-P-K producer levered to the nitrogen price rally with less single-plant risk.
Captures the lagged grain-price firming from reduced global fertilizer use.
Cross-domain hedge on the energy-security-driven nuclear reacceleration.

title: OPEC+ fully unwinds cuts, flooding barrels and lifting crude-tanker ton-miles
hypothesis: Continued acceleration of OPEC+ production returns creates crude oversupply and contango, boosting VLCC voyage and floating-storage demand -- the inverse of the classic output-cut bear case.

chain.cause: OPEC+ returns barrels faster than demand absorbs them
chain.effect: Rising export volumes and contango-driven floating storage tighten VLCC availability, spiking crude-tanker rates
chain.rationale: More barrels over long Gulf-to-Asia routes plus storage demand is directly bullish VLCC owners, the opposite of the intuitive output-cut bearish reflex.

chain.cause: Oversupply pushes crude prices lower across the energy complex
chain.effect: Cheaper fossil energy modestly dampens near-term urgency in competing energy sentiment
chain.rationale: Lower oil prices soften the broad energy-scarcity narrative; a mild sentiment headwind for uranium, noted as context only.

playbook.rationale: Pure VLCC exposure benefits directly from higher volumes and storage demand.
High-beta VLCC fleet with strong payout captures the rate spike.
Diversified crude/product fleet participates with lower volatility.
